title: Tenant-aware ingest circuit and typed telemetry bridge
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem: The current usage-event ingestion path validates envelope shapes at a global, best-effort level. This causes two problems for high-throughput Console tenants: 1) noisy strict rejections for backward-compatible schema changes (breaking downstream dashboards), and 2) uneven latency/throughput characteristics for tenant bursts because validation is monolithic and not tenant-aware. We also lack a robust fallback so when validation spikes, events sometimes inflight-drop or cause consumer backpressure.

Goal: Build a tenant-aware ingest circuit and a "typed telemetry bridge" that provides per-tenant validation policies (strict / soft-coerce / passthrough), computes a schema-drift score, and exposes a circuit-breaker style routing decision that can divert failing traffic to a degraded but durable path with lineage tags. The system should minimize tail-latency impact, preserve downstream analytic correctness where possible, and enable safe incremental rollout for critical customers.

High-level approach:
- Introduce a lightweight "typed envelope" layer at the ingress broker that extracts route keys (tenant_id, source, route_version) and an event fingerprint. Implement a fast path: if event schema hash matches tenant's pinned schema or falls within an allowed compatibility set, forward to primary topic with minimal validation (header checks + checksum).
- Compute a per-event schema-drift score using a configurable ruleset (field presence, type mismatch counts, enum divergence). Maintain a short-lived moving-window per-tenant drift metric; when it exceeds the tenant threshold, trip a tenant-level circuit.
- Circuit actions: when tripped, route to one of three configurable degradation paths: 1) soft-coerce and forward (attempt safe type coercions / default fills), 2) drop-to-raw-topic (raw-event bucket for manual reconciliation), 3) slow-path validation with sampled processing (forensics). Default behavior is soft-coerce then tag with lineage.reason="soft_coerce".
- Persist lineage tags and original envelope_id for downstream reconciliation and replay tooling.
- Expose per-tenant policy APIs (Console + k8s-configmap for Private) so platform and PM teams can set strictness and thresholds.

Design decisions / trade-offs:
- Soft-coercion rules: prefer non-destructive coercions (string->enum via mapping table, number-string tolerant cast). We avoid heuristic field reshaping (object->array) for now to limit data confusion.
- Move heavy validation to async workers where possible; only run light-weight deterministic checks on the ingest path to keep p95 ingest latency under goal (<35ms additional overhead).
- Keep compatibility with existing downstream consumers by adding a new envelope header X-Redwood-Schema-Policy instead of replacing existing topics.

Implementation plan (workstreams):
1) Ingest Broker: extend existing broker with typed-envelope extractor and per-tenant policy cache (LRU, ttl). Feature-flag the new path.
2) Drift Engine: small streaming job that computes schema-drift scores per tenant and writes to metadata store (etcd or Dynamo). Exposes API for circuit controller.
3) Circuit Controller: evaluates drift metric vs policy and updates per-tenant state; publishes events and metrics.
4) Degradation Workers: implement soft-coerce plugin and raw-topic sink with enriched lineage metadata.
5) Migration scripts: policy defaults (P0 tenants strict=false), and backfill tooling to tag historical events for audits.

Testing & observability:
- Unit and property tests for soft-coercion rules (edge inputs), fuzz tests for envelope parsing.
- Perf microbenchmarks for typed-envelope path vs baseline (<5% throughput degradation target).
- Dashboards and alerts: validation_failure_rate, schema_drift_score_per_tenant, circuit_tripped_count, spilled_event_count, ingest_p95_latency, degraded_path_latency.
- SLOs: keep platform-level ingest latency increase <35ms p95; developer-visible event loss = 0 for strict mode (we only drop to raw-topic, no deletions).

Rollout plan:
- Feature flag + opt-in for 10% tenant canary (by activity + low-risk tenants) for 2 days.
- Evaluate metrics and manual verification with Support/PM on a set of sample dashboards.
- Gradual growth to 50% then all tenants, with policy defaults applied and exceptions handled via config.
- Finalize docs, API schemas, and a Console UI to view/troubleshoot tripped circuits.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end pipeline passes canary with no >2% increase in p95 latency across canary tenants.
- Soft-coercion tests cover >95% of our sampled schema drift cases and have explicit reversible mapping tables.
- Runbook for a tripped circuit exists and is validated by SRE (playbook in Confluence).
- PRs merged and a canary tag deployed to runtime; dashboards show expected metrics.

Open questions / risks:
- Storage choice for per-tenant state (etcd vs Dynamo) — latency vs operational cost trade-off.
- Policy UX for enterprise customers: need an audit+consent flow for automatic coercions.
- Edge cases where coercion may mask data corruption; require retention of original raw events for 90 days.
comments: 2026-01-13 — Asha Kapoor: Initial triage done. Spike to measure overhead of typed-envelope extraction (see /docs/spikes/ingest-typed-envelope.md). Preliminary numbers: ~12% p95 CPU on broker in local cluster. Will propose optimizations (off-heap parsing and mempool).

2026-01-18 — Liam Ortega: Completed spike + bench. Implementing fast path that only checks 3 header fields reduces CPU to ~4% impact at p95 in bench. Creating RFC for soft-coercion rules: https://confluence.internal.redwood/TelemetryBridgeRFC
2026-01-22 — Maya Patel (PM): Verified canary cohort selection criteria. Request to add tenant opt-out via Console settings. Added ticket to backlog for Console UI (PM-423).

2026-02-02 — Security Review (Rajiv Menon): Noted that raw-topic contains PII risk. Recommend encrypt-at-rest keys rotation and KMS tagging for raw sinks. Added security requirement to release checklist.

2026-02-15 — Liam Ortega: Deployed circuit controller prototype to staging; observed drift spikes correlated with SDK v2.3 rollout. Circuit tripped for 3 tenants and routed to soft-coerce path successfully. Raising a minor follow-up to add more conservative mapping tables.
2026-02-24 — SRE (Elena Ruiz): Load test results attached to PR; ingestion p95 increased by 28ms in synthetic 2x burst. Within our 35ms threshold. Ready for canary deployment next week.
